analysis:
Examined the two supplied units of .github/workflows/release-provider.yml. The visible changes are: header comments documenting the *_CLUSTER_RUNTIME_ENABLED repository variables (head lines 66-72), and a new CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND env in the build-and-release job (head 298-308). The expression requires publish=='true' and matches the environment to the corresponding repository variable. These are non-secret vars, and the value is derived from resolve-env outputs, not from caller or PR-controlled free text. Other changed ranges (head 941-1023, 1078-1088) are not in the supplied head text, and the patch excerpt is truncated, so the new step content there was not reviewed. The base unit (lines 1061-1296) shows the existing stage-release and publish-release jobs. They use per-environment secret gating, with PROD and LEGACY values empty unless the environment is prod, artifact id and digest pinned downloads, and no persist-credentials. The head hunk at 1078-1088 appears to correspond to the base's legacy-secret fallback loop. Base 977-978 changed, but that range is not visible in the supplied base unit.

No regression is identified in the visible content. The new flag only controls whether cluster_runtime facts are included in the release registration payload. Security-relevant pieces that were not visible include: how scripts/provider-release-publication.py or the build-and-release steps consume CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND and compute cluster_runtime from the final signed app; whether failure semantics are fail-closed when enabled; and whether the coordinator validates the block. This touches the release/qualification trust chain (A-011, A-017, T-034, T-054), but the supplied evidence does not show a weakening. The integration pass should examine head 941-1023, which adds the computation step and is not visible here. The provided T-041 definition concerns the prefix cache and is not affected by this CI change.
